ns2:section.sectionText: Military Veterans: Community Health & Wellness is a course designed to educate students on the dominant factors impacting Military/Veteran communities today. The course begins with an immersion into Military/Veteran culture (military entrance such as how and why people join, branch differences and missions, structure, hierarchy and rank, population demographics, organizational characteristics) before examining prominent community health issues impacting Military/Veteran cohorts and communities at large. Issues explored include military transitions and reintegration, suicide & mental health, Military Sexual Trauma, food insecurity and nutrition, substance abuse, and homelessness. This course will include a service-learning component. Class will meet in room 1020 at the Chez Center for Wounded Veterans in Higher Education, 908 W. Nevada St., Urbana.
